C1.worst_defect: The hero explains the product in developer terms ("the open-source headless commerce framework") and does not say what a counter needs (a browser on desktop Chrome, a card terminal you already own, no cash-drawer kick). That only appears in the last section, "Before you start", so a shop owner cannot tell at a glance whether their counter setup will work.
C1.where: home/desktop/01 hero paragraph; home/desktop/02 'Before you start'

C2.worst_defect: The home page claims "keeps selling when the connection drops" (hero and the 'Keeps selling offline' card) but leaves out the condition from At the till: "Keep the till's tab open while the connection is down ... a reload, or closing and reopening the browser, needs the connection to load the till again". The headline promise is wider than what the product actually does.
C2.where: home/desktop/01 'Keeps selling offline' card vs at-the-till/desktop/03 'If the internet drops'

C3.worst_defect: Step 5 puts the .env line "CORS_ORIGINS=https://app.vendurepos.com" in a code block labelled "Terminal", so it reads as a command to run when it is a line to add to the .env file. Separately, the device-key option needs ReadOrder added by hand ("add ReadOrder to that role yourself"), which is easy to miss when handing the job to a freelancer.
C3.where: quick-start/desktop/02 step 5 Terminal block; quick-start text 'Optional: a device key for each till'

C4.worst_defect: The section a shop owner most needs, "If the internet drops", is a single eight-sentence paragraph. Its key instructions (keep the tab open, don't clear site data, watch "N orders waiting to send") sit mid-paragraph rather than as a short list. Also, "Refund a sale" is a 1./2. numbered list whose items are not sequential steps.
C4.where: at-the-till/desktop/03 'If the internet drops'; at-the-till/desktop/02 'Refund a sale'

C5.worst_defect: The hero till screenshot is cut off mid-row at its bottom edge: a fourth row of product tiles shows only their coloured tops. The image looks cropped rather than composed.
C5.where: home/desktop/01 hero screenshot bottom edge (~y 1140); same in home.desktop-dark

C6.worst_defect: In the phone hero screenshot, the till's cart column header is truncated to "Q..." next to ITEM/TOTAL. This is the first product image a phone reader sees, and it shows a clipped header.

C7.worst_defect: The share card's till screenshot runs off the bottom edge, cutting product tiles and the "Add charge" button in half. Everything else checks out: Lighthouse 98/100/100/100, the 404 page returns status 404, and llms.txt, sitemap, robots and search all respond.

overall_worst.defect: The home page promises the till "keeps selling when the connection drops" without the condition that staff must not reload or close the tab while offline: the till cannot load again until the connection returns. A cashier who refreshes during an outage loses the till mid-shift, and the owner only learns this from a paragraph deep in At the till.
overall_worst.where: home/desktop/01 hero and 'Keeps selling offline' card; condition only in at-the-till/desktop/03 'If the internet drops'
overall_worst.fix: Add one sentence to the home 'Keeps selling offline' card: "Keep the till's tab open: a reload or browser restart needs the connection back." Repeat it as the first bullet of a short list at the top of 'If the internet drops'.
